vedic_reference.note: Ronav is a modern form of the ancient name Rudra, who is the god of storms and destruction in Hindu mythology. He is also known as Mahadeva, Shiva, and Pashupati.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ronav was a famous Jain Tirthankara who lived around 11th century BCE. The name Ronav carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that emphasizes nonviolence, or ahimsa, and self-control, or tapas. Tirthankaras are the spiritual teachers and guides in Jainism. Ronav is one of the 24 Tirthankaras.

historical_references.reference: Ronav is also mentioned in Hindu mythology as the father of the sage Kashyapa, who was the father of the Devas (gods) and Asuras (demons). This Ronav is believed to have lived around 5000 BCE.
historical_references.context: In Hindu mythology, there are various creation stories, and one of them involves the god Brahma creating Prajapati, who then creates a sister-wife named Prakriti. Their son is named Ronav, and he marries his sister-wife Swaha. Their son Kashyapa then goes on to father both the Devas and Asuras.

On social media, parents and name enthusiasts often discuss and share the significance and origin of the name. Personal blogs and websites dedicated to Indian culture and baby names also feature 'Ronav' as a popular choice due to its rich history and meaning. Additionally, some parents may choose the name 'Ronav' for their children as a tribute to their Indian heritage or as a reflection of their desire for their child to be adventurous and explorative.
